item: HCR-9 (step 4: the MMR re-cut, measured on near-duplicate clusters)
method: bench/mmr_eval.py, one process per space. Three corpora per run: 'organic' (the corpus as it is, HCR-8's 347 held-out questions), 'competitor' (plus two re-captures of each sampled question's strongest wrong competitor) and 'target' (plus two re-captures of each sampled question's target). The competitor of a question is the best-ranked memory that is not a right answer, pooled over tuned lean and tuned high with the re-cut off. Sampling: 25 questions per corpus, seed 20261127. Re-captures: written by a language model (Claude, three writers, one per corpus) shown only the first ~2,500 characters of the memory, as a terse note and as a short narrative, under a new name, 81 to 150 words. All re-captures of a condition are in the corpus at once. Scoring: plain recall() top 10; a right answer is the target, any memory the pooled judging accepted, or (target condition) a re-capture of the target. lean ran on description rows (what it ships), high on whole-memory rows, each at its committed floor and gate as of this run.
corpus_labels: hippo = hippo's own corpus; corpus-b and corpus-c are two private project corpora of 113 and 1,070 indexed memories
arms: v1.48: lambda 0.8 on the raw fused score. off: lambda 1.0. pool-scaled: relevance min-max scaled over the re-cut's pool (recall_rank._mmr_relevance), at lambda 0.8, 0.6, 0.4, 0.3 and 0.2.
summary: What was asked: HCR-8 could count what the MMR re-cut costs (one target per question) and not what it is for. This set adds near-duplicates: for 75 held-out questions (25 per corpus), two re-captures of the target memory and two of its strongest wrong competitor, written by a model shown only that memory. 274 re-captures; their cosine to the memory they re-capture runs 0.555 to 0.954 on bge-small (median about 0.82) and 0.648 to 0.97 on the 4B (median about 0.87).

The re-cut as v1.48 shipped it does remove duplicates, and loses right answers doing it, even where it should help. With the competitors' re-captures in the corpus it takes -0.747 [-0.96, -0.5333] competitor rows out of the top 10 on lean and -1.213 [-1.4, -1.0267] on high, and the right answer leaves the top 5 more often: -0.107 [-0.1867, -0.0267] lean, -0.080 [-0.1467, -0.0267] high. On the corpora as they are (347 questions): -0.0461 [-0.0749, -0.0202] hits lean, -0.0432 [-0.0692, -0.0173] high.

Why: the relevance term was the raw fused score (reciprocal-rank sums near 0.02) against a cosine near 0.7, so at lambda 0.8 the diversity term outweighed relevance about nine to one. After the first pick the order was set by dissimilarity.

With relevance scaled to the pool (best 1.0, worst 0.0) lambda is a weight, and there is a setting that costs nothing measured. Lambda 0.4, against the re-cut off: organic hits +0.0000 [-0.0086, 0.0086] lean (302 of 347) and +0.0029 [-0.0058, 0.0144] high (336 of 347); hit@5 -0.003 [-0.0086, 0.0] and -0.006 [-0.0144, 0.0]; MRR -0.0027 [-0.0057, 0.0001] and -0.0023 [-0.0064, 0.0014]. Every interval includes zero.

What lambda 0.4 still buys: when a fact was saved three times, its rows in the top 5 fall -0.507 [-0.68, -0.3467] on high (from 2.533) and -0.200 [-0.2933, -0.1067] on lean (from 2.227); a competitor saved three times loses -0.547 [-0.6933, -0.4] rows of the top 10 on high and -0.093 [-0.1733, -0.0133] on lean. That is about four tenths of what the v1.48 re-cut removed on high and under two tenths on lean (bge-small's cosines sit closer together, so the same weight moves less), with no right answer lost for it.

Lambda 0.3 removes more (-0.973 [-1.16, -0.7733] right rows in the top 5 on high) and costs the 4B a resolved -0.012 [-0.0231, -0.0029] of hit@5 on the corpora as they are; 0.2 costs it more (hit@5 -0.026 [-0.0432, -0.0086]). 0.6 and 0.8 cost nothing and remove almost nothing.

Decision: the re-cut stays, rescaled. recall_rank._MMR_NORMALIZE is on and _MMR_LAMBDA is 0.4, on every profile. HIPPO_MMR_LAMBDA still overrides it and 1.0 still turns the re-cut off; the number now weighs the pool-scaled score.
caveats: Re-captures are a model's, written from the head of each memory; real duplicates may sit closer or further.

75 sampled questions: an interval on a hit rate there is about +/- 0.10 wide, so 'no loss' in the duplicate conditions means none this set could resolve. The organic condition (347 questions) carries the cost side.
Every re-capture of a condition is in the corpus together (94 to 100 added notes per corpus), which changes a 108-memory corpus more than a 1,070-memory one.
Plain recall() is scored, not the prompt hook.

lean.note: counts and intervals only, no query and no memory name. Intervals are 95%: Wilson for a hit rate, percentile bootstrap (2000 resamples) for a mean and for every paired difference.

high.note: counts and intervals only, no query and no memory name. Intervals are 95%: Wilson for a hit rate, percentile bootstrap (2000 resamples) for a mean and for every paired difference.
